faqs.question: What is GRAND-EOS™?
faqs.answer: GRAND-EOS™ is a continuously tunable hyperspectral camera from Photon etc. that operates from 400 to 1650 nm and combines micro and macro imaging modalities.

faqs.question: What wavelength range does GRAND-EOS™ cover?
faqs.answer: GRAND-EOS™ is continuously tunable from 400 to 1650 nm.

faqs.question: What is GRAND-EOS™ used for?
faqs.answer: GRAND-EOS™ is designed for hyperspectral imaging applications including photovoltaic material characterization, counterfeit product identification, forensic analysis, food sorting and environmental sorting.

faqs.question: What is a hyperspectral data cube?
faqs.answer: A hyperspectral data cube combines spatial and spectral information. In GRAND-EOS™, spatial information is represented along the X-Y axes and spectral information along the Z-axis.

faqs.question: Does GRAND-EOS™ require image reconstruction?
faqs.answer: No. Photon etc.'s global-imaging technology extracts a hyperspectral data cube from a handful of monochromatic images without the need for image reconstruction.

faqs.question: Can GRAND-EOS™ perform reflectance imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. GRAND-EOS™ is designed for reflectance imaging.

faqs.question: Can GRAND-EOS™ perform transmittance imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. Transmittance imaging is one of the supported imaging modes.

faqs.question: Can GRAND-EOS™ perform luminescence imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. GRAND-EOS™ is designed for luminescence imaging.

faqs.question: Does GRAND-EOS™ support both micro and macro imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. GRAND-EOS™ combines micro and macro imaging modalities in one platform.

faqs.question: Can the field of view be adjusted?
faqs.answer: Yes. The field of view can be adjusted depending on the application and sample size.

faqs.question: What filtering technology does GRAND-EOS™ use?
faqs.answer: GRAND-EOS™ uses Photon etc.'s patented filtering technology based on volume Bragg grating (VBG).

faqs.question: Does GRAND-EOS™ use polarized wavelength selection?
What are the main applications of GRAND-EOS™?
faqs.answer: Photon etc. identifies photovoltaic material characterization, counterfeit product identification, forensic analysis, food sorting and environmental sorting as application areas.

faqs.question: Is GRAND-EOS™ suitable for industrial applications?
faqs.answer: Yes. GRAND-EOS™ is designed for both fundamental research and industrial applications.

faqs.question: What is the difference between GRAND-EOS™ and IMA™?
faqs.answer: IMA™ is primarily a hyperspectral microscopy platform for microscopic material characterization, while GRAND-EOS™ combines micro and macro hyperspectral imaging and is designed as an area-scan imaging platform with continuous tuning from 400 to 1650 nm.

longForm.heroLead: Connect micro- and macro-scale imaging with continuously tunable hyperspectral analysis. Photon etc. GRAND-EOS™ is a global hyperspectral camera continuously tunable from 400 to 1650 nm. It combines micro and macro imaging modalities in one platform, allowing researchers and industrial users to analyze samples across different scales. Using Photon etc.'s patented volume Bragg grating (VBG) filtering technology, GRAND-EOS™ provides non-polarized wavelength selection with high throughput and efficiency. The system generates a hyperspectral data cube containing spatial information along the X-Y axes and spectral information along the Z-axis. Photon etc.'s global imaging technology extracts this data cube from a small number of monochromatic images without requiring image reconstruction. GRAND-EOS™ supports reflectance, transmittance and luminescence imaging, with an adjustable field of view based on the application and sample size.

sections.title: How GRAND-EOS™ Works
body: GRAND-EOS™ uses Photon etc.'s patented global-imaging technology to extract a hyperspectral data cube from a handful of monochromatic images.
The workflow: Sample → Monochromatic images → Global imaging acquisition → Hyperspectral data cube → Spatial + spectral analysis.
A key part of the GRAND-EOS™ approach is that the data cube is generated without the need for image reconstruction.

A conventional image provides information about where features are located; a hyperspectral data cube adds spectral information to every spatial location, enabling users to examine spectral differences across different regions of a sample.

sections.title: Three Ways to Capture Spectral Information
sections.description: GRAND-EOS™ supports three major imaging approaches, each suited to different sample properties.

steps.title: Reflectance Imaging
steps.description: Captures spectral information from light reflected by the sample.

steps.title: Transmittance Imaging
steps.description: Captures spectral information from light transmitted through the sample.

steps.title: Luminescence Imaging
steps.description: Captures spectral information from light emitted by the sample.

sections.disclaimer: The appropriate imaging mode depends on the optical properties of the sample and the intended research or industrial workflow.
